cards.title: 'I'll remember' is not a reminder system
cards.body: Busy mornings, TV serials, a guest at the door. Even sharp memories slip. A phone set up properly does the remembering for them.

cards.title: Use the alarm they already know
cards.body: The built-in clock app is often easier than a new app. Set one alarm per dose time, not one per tablet.

cards.title: Label every alarm clearly
cards.body: Name it 'Morning BP tablet, after breakfast' instead of leaving just a time. Specific words are easier to act on.

cards.title: Turn the volume up, then test
cards.body: Alarm volume is often separate from ringer volume. Pick a loud, distinct tone and test it from the next room.

cards.title: Pair alarms with a daily habit
cards.body: Morning chai, lunch, the evening news. Linking a dose to something that already happens makes it stick.

cards.title: Check in, don't police
cards.body: A quick 'did the 9 pm one ring?' call is enough. Agree on it together so it feels like teamwork, not surveillance.

cards.title: Update when the prescription changes
cards.body: New doctor visit, new timings. Update the alarms the same day. AICA is building dose reminders that understand 1-0-1 and half tablets.

takeaway: Use labelled, loud alarms tied to daily habits, check in kindly, and update them every time the prescription changes.
share: Set up medicine alarms on Mummy's phone. Label them, make them loud, tie them to chai time.
